_README: Your judgments about specific events. Two things happen to each entry:
1. OVERRIDE - if an event matching `match` is in the window, its score is
replaced by yours. Immediate, exact, and it beats the model every time.
2. CALIBRATION - entries are also shown to the scorer as worked examples,
so the same judgment generalises to events you have never rated.
That second part is the point. Abstract rubric instructions moved the model
very little (three attempts at the Pride ranking barely shifted it), but
concrete examples of how THIS family scores THIS event are a much stronger
match         substring, matched case-insensitively against the title.
Keep it specific enough not to catch unrelated events.
family_fit    0-100, or null to leave the model's score alone
why           one line, in your words. This is what the scorer reads,
so say the REASON, not just the number: 'huge festival,
lots to do' generalises, 'should be higher' does not.
added         YYYY-MM-DD, so stale entries can be pruned later

events.why: Huge street festival with tons going on - stages, food, crowds. A great family day out, not an adults-only event.
Fun but not special - this promotion runs every month in many cities, so it is never a reason to plan a weekend around.
